name: Reduced-Residence Naturalization for a Spouse of a Cuban Citizen

requirements.blocker_text: Cuba's new Ley de Ciudadania reduces the naturalization residence requirement from the standard 5 years to 2 years for the spouse, parent, or child of a Cuban citizen by birth, provided the applicant holds Permanent Resident classification for that period. There is no automatic acquisition of citizenship purely from the marriage itself -- this is a reduced-threshold NATURALIZATION, not a distinct marriage-based route. The same age, character (no convictions for terrorism, trafficking, money laundering, or related offenses), social-integration, and citizenship-exam conditions apply as for standard naturalization.
requirements.fix_path: Marry a Cuban citizen, obtain Permanent Resident classification, hold it for 2 years, pass the citizenship exam, and apply.

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 2 years Permanent Resident classification (reduced from the standard 5)

sources.title: CubaTramite (immigration-consultancy guide) -- naturalization thresholds, the 2-year spousal reduction, character conditions, dual-citizenship policy

GENUINE FINDING: like Kosovo and Mali built earlier in this dataset, Cuba's marriage 'route' is a reduced-residence naturalization variant, not an automatic or optional acquisition mechanism. dual_citizenship_allowed set to true, matching the standard naturalization case -- see cu_citizenship_naturalisation.json for the one confirmed exception (the discretionary 'exceptional interest' track, which does require surrendering the prior nationality's documents).
